props.title: I Married a Witch
props.initialSlug: Bewitched woman falls for descendant of her accuser

sections.content: I Married a Witch (1942) blazed the trail for supernatural romantic comedies, influencing everything from Bewitched (1964-1972) to Bell, Book and Candle (1958). Veronica Lake sparkles as Jennifer, a witch who falls for the descendant of her Puritan persecutor - her revenge plot deliciously backfiring through love. Director René Clair brings his French poetic realism touch to Hollywood screwball comedy, creating magical effects that still charm 80+ years later. The film's playful blend of romance and witchcraft established core genre elements we'd later see in Practical Magic (1998) and The Love Witch (2016).

sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond just witch-themed stories. Its screwball comedy DNA shares strands with Bringing Up Baby (1938) and The Lady Eve (1941) - particularly in how supernatural elements drive misunderstandings and romantic complications. The special effects, while simple by today's standards, were groundbreaking for 1942, especially the smoke-based transformation sequences that would influence supernatural films for decades to come.

Lake's portrayal of Jennifer set the template for the "magical woman disrupting a man's life" trope that would dominate supernatural romance for decades. You can trace direct lines from her performance to Elizabeth Montgomery in Bewitched and even Michelle Pfeiffer in The Witches of Eastwick (1987). The film's sharp critique of political corruption and marriage feels surprisingly modern, wrapped in its supernatural screwball package. SUBHEAD: Legacy and Modern Interpretations

sections.content: Contemporary witch-themed romantic comedies like Teen Witch (1989) and Hocus Pocus (1993) owe clear debts to I Married a Witch's blend of magic and romance. The film's core concept - supernatural beings navigating human love - continues through modern variations like Warm Bodies (2013) and Good Omens (2019), showing how versatile and enduring its basic template remains.
